A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite retitling and renaming UHead to ReProbe. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. The blank cells in v1's beam-search Table 6 are visible in the original document, rather than extraction gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original step-verification and decoding experiments with Qwen3-8B and Phi-4, training-data analyses, and human validation of the annotation pipeline.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds hidden-state probes, native-thinking evaluation, architecture ablations, reasoning-length analysis, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: V3 adds probes using hidden states from all layers and sentence-based step extraction for native thinking. It also specifies attention over five preceding tokens, versus v1's 1–3. These extend the inputs and processing procedure; the frozen backbone and projection/Transformer/pooling/classifier architecture remain.

E1.justification: The PRM800K training source and eight mathematical, planning, and QA benchmarks remain. V3 adds a distinct native-thinking scenario involving long, unformatted reasoning traces requiring sentence segmentation (Appendix A.2), extending beyond the formatted CoT scenario without adding domains or datasets.

E2.justification: The corresponding Qwen3 and Phi-4 best-of-N tables remove the entire non-voting uncertainty-baseline block: MinNumberofSteps, MaxProb, MaxEntropy, and Perplexity (v1 Tables 3/8; v3 Tables 3/7). Majority voting and the PRM comparators remain. This substantially narrows comparison against lightweight alternatives, although the original step-verification comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: V1's main online experiment greedily retains one of five continuations; v3 specifies beam search with B=5 and N=5. V1 already contains limited beam-search results, so this is an expanded and revised evaluation rather than an entirely new search setting. Native-thinking evaluation adds Qwen3-1.7B, GPT-OSS-120B sentence-wise annotation, and a 1024-token training limit. New analyses introduce length-binned ROC-AUC and batch-size-one timing on 500 MATH samples.

E4.justification: V3 adds architecture ablations comparing step-level Transformer probes with token-level Transformer and linear probes (Table 9), reasoning-length analysis (Figure 6), and computational-efficiency measurements (Table 10). PRM fusion, training-data quantity/diversity, and best-of-N sample-scaling analyses already existed in v1 and are largely retained or redisplayed.

E5.justification: Both versions state that training, evaluation, and sampling use fixed seeds of 1 or 42 and discuss API nondeterminism. Neither reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; v3 does not introduce a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original attention/logit step-verification scores and retained best-of-N rows remain unchanged. V3 adds hidden-state results, including 0.604 overall PR-AUC for self-annotation in Table 1, and native-thinking results with 0.447 overall PR-AUC in Table 8. Beam-search results are expanded and revised, while greedy-online and several best-of-N baseline results disappear. Architecture, length, and runtime findings are also new; changed beam scores should not be interpreted as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: V3 adds Appendix E's formal time and memory complexity analysis, including step-length definitions, the bound sum(m_s squared) <= m_max*T, and an argument contrasting step-local probe computation with full-trace PRM attention. V1 has no corresponding derivation. V3 also formally describes beam-set expansion and selection beyond v1's greedy online equations.

C1.justification: The central claims remain lightweight verification from frozen LLM internals, automatic or self-generated supervision, competitiveness with much larger PRMs, and cross-domain generalization. Both versions already claim usefulness for test-time scaling and complementary fusion with PRMs. The new title and probing terminology primarily reframe these retained contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds qualifications about stronger relative performance on short reasoning chains and comparable performance on longer chains. It explains runtime differences through implementation choices and the incompatibility of attention-map extraction with efficient attention implementations. The substantive limitations concerning model-specific probes and restricted training-data diversity remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds native-thinking generation and annotation prompts, sentence-wise labeling instructions, explicit weighted binary-cross-entropy training, and detailed timing boundaries. Appendix B.3 newly reports approximately 4 versus 32 GH200 GPU-hours for hidden-state versus attention/logit probes and annotation/evaluation costs. Core hyperparameters remain unchanged. The new approximately $200 training-annotation figure is unreconciled with the retained greater-than-$2,000 statement in Limitations.

R1.justification: V3 adds references including Su et al. (2024), Xie et al. (2023), and Vazhentsev et al. (2025), while dropping broader uncertainty and CoT-faithfulness references. It foregrounds reasoning probes instead of repeatedly describing an extension of UHead, but still cites Shelmanov et al.'s framework. The main positioning against PRMs, unsupervised uncertainty methods, and formal verification remains.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the introduction, background, and method exposition, changes the title and terminology, separates Main Results from Analysis, moves baseline details into the appendix, and brings limitations into the main document. These are extensive narrative and organizational revisions beyond additions of scientific content.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column presentation. Figure 1 is comprehensively redrawn, a new test-time-scaling schematic is added, and existing scaling panels are consolidated and reformatted. Tables gain probe variants and new analyses, while human-validation results move to the appendix. The visual revision extends well beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens scrutiny of the approach through native-thinking evaluation, architecture and length analyses, and direct runtime measurements that v1 lacked. These improve support for applicability and efficiency. However, removing useful cheap comparators weakens the best-of-N evidence: v1 Table 3 reports 23.4% Trips accuracy for MinNumberofSteps versus 17.2% for the best UHead, and that comparator disappears in v3. Together with unreconciled annotation-cost statements, this limits the net quality gain despite substantial additions.
